description: Golden Record CaseData bundle for Contact Center Knowledge-Based Coach POC. Each case includes anonymized raw ticket text plus SME annotations (correct SOP steps, objectives, constraints).

cases.raw_content:
Customer: I want a refund NOW. This is ridiculous.
Agent: We can't do that.
Customer: Are you kidding me? I will cancel everything.
Agent: That's the policy.
Customer: Then get me a manager. I'm done.

learning_objectives: Show empathy before policy
Ask clarifying questions (date/plan)
Offer approved alternatives without sounding dismissive
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge frustration and apologize
Verify transaction date and subscription plan
Explain refund policy clearly before refusal
Offer approved alternatives (partial credit or escalation path)
policy_constraints: Do not promise a full refund if outside the refund window
Do not offer compensation above $20 credit without approval
resolution_criteria: Customer accepts a policy-compliant alternative OR agrees to escalation
Customer tone de-escalates by end of interaction

cases.raw_content:
Customer: I can't log in. It says 'invalid code' every time.
Agent: Reset your password.
Customer: I did, three times. Still broken.
Agent: Try later.
Customer: I need access for work right now.

learning_objectives: Collect key diagnostic details early
Provide one step at a time and confirm outcome
Escalate with complete context if unresolved
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge impact and urgency
Gather details (device, browser, MFA/OTP, timestamp, error text)
Try safe quick fixes (incognito, time sync, resend code)
Escalate with required logs/timestamps if persists
common_mistakes_to_avoid: Repeating generic steps without new info
policy_constraints: Do not request passwords or full OTP codes
Do not ask for sensitive personal identifiers
resolution_criteria: Issue resolved OR clean escalation created with complete diagnostic info

cases.raw_content:
Customer: My delivery is late AGAIN.
Agent: It will arrive soon.
Customer: You said that yesterday too. Where is it?
Agent: It's with the courier.
Customer: That's not an answer. Give me a real update or refund me.

learning_objectives: Validate frustration about repeat delays
Provide concrete tracking info and ETA
Offer policy-aligned options if outside SLA
correct_sop_steps: Apologize and acknowledge repeat delay
Check tracking status and last scan event
Provide updated ETA with confidence level
Offer approved options (replacement, escalation, refund if eligible)
common_mistakes_to_avoid: No timeline or next update commitment
policy_constraints: Replacement allowed only if no movement for 48 hours
Refund allowed if past SLA by 3 business days
resolution_criteria: Customer receives a concrete next step with timeline
Customer chooses an option and agrees

cases.raw_content:
Customer: Cancel my plan. I'm done.
Agent: Why?
Customer: Too expensive and support is useless.
Agent: Okay canceling.
Customer: Wait—when does it end and will I be charged again?

learning_objectives: Respect cancellation intent without interrogating
Offer one retention option once (not pushy)
Confirm end date, charges, and confirmation
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge request and confirm you can help
Ask one optional feedback question
Offer one approved retention option if eligible (pause/discount)
Confirm cancellation timing, billing impact, and send confirmation
policy_constraints: Offer discount only if tenure >= 6 months
Do not promise refunds for past months
resolution_criteria: Customer confirms they understand end date/charges

cases.raw_content:
Customer: Your service is down. My team is blocked.
Agent: Not sure.
Customer: This is costing us money. What's the ETA?
Agent: I think it'll be back soon.
Customer: 'Think'? I need facts and updates.

learning_objectives: Acknowledge severity and take ownership
Avoid speculation; give status + next update time
Offer workaround/escalation for critical impact
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge incident impact and apologize
Confirm if incident is known and share official status reference
Commit to next update time (even if no ETA)
Offer workaround and escalation path for critical customers
policy_constraints: Do not provide an ETA unless confirmed by incident lead
Do not share internal system names
resolution_criteria: Customer receives update cadence and reference

cases.raw_content:
Customer: My card keeps getting declined, but the bank says it's fine.
Agent: Then it's your bank.
Customer: It's not. I used the same card elsewhere. Fix it.
Agent: Try another card.
Customer: I need this purchase to go through today.

learning_objectives: Avoid blame; take ownership and gather details
Check for common causes (AVS mismatch, limits, retries, region)
Provide safe steps and escalation path
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge urgency and apologize for the friction
Collect details (error message, last 4 digits optional, billing ZIP match, time, attempts, country)
Suggest safe steps (wait 10 min, confirm billing address, try once, alternate method like PayPal if supported)
Escalate to payments team with timestamp/error and advise customer of next update
policy_constraints: Do not request full card number or CVV
Do not store payment details in chat
resolution_criteria: Customer gets clear next steps (safe retry) OR escalation with expected timeline

cases.raw_content:
Customer: I requested a password reset but the email never comes.
Agent: Check your spam.
Customer: I did. Nothing.
Agent: Then wait.
Customer: I can't wait. I'm locked out and I have a deadline.

learning_objectives: Guide step-by-step without repeating generic advice
Check common deliverability causes (filters, domain, typos)
Offer alternative verification/escalation if stuck
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge urgency and apologize
Confirm email address format (without asking for sensitive info) and ask about corporate email filtering
Suggest whitelisted sender domain + try resend + alternate browser/device
If still failing, offer escalation and an alternative verification path (if policy allows)
policy_constraints: Do not disclose whether an email exists in the system beyond what the customer provides
resolution_criteria: Email deliverability issue resolved OR escalation created with required context
Customer has a concrete next action

cases.raw_content:
Customer: You charged me twice. I'm filing a chargeback.
Agent: We didn't.
Customer: Yes you did. I see two charges pending.
Agent: That's not possible.
Customer: I'm taking this to my bank if you don't fix it now.

learning_objectives: Avoid contradicting; validate concern and investigate
Explain pending vs posted charges clearly
Offer concrete actions and escalation path
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge concern and apologize
Gather transaction details safely (dates/amounts/merchant descriptor; no full card info)
Explain pending authorization vs posted charges and expected timelines
If true duplicate charge: initiate refund/void process or escalate with timeline
common_mistakes_to_avoid: Arguing about what the customer sees
policy_constraints: Do not request full card details
Do not guarantee immediate reversal if pending authorization
resolution_criteria: Customer understands the situation (pending vs posted) OR duplicate identified and action taken
Chargeback threat de-escalates or is handled with clear next steps
